How to Respond to Apartment Reviews: Examples for Positive, Negative and Fake Reviews

Nov 2, 2026Michael Shad, Founder of The SocialDM6 min read
Key takeaways
  • Reply to every review, briefly, including five star ratings with no text.
  • Never confirm someone is a resident, share private details, argue or admit legal liability in a public reply.
  • You can flag reviews that break Google policy, such as fake engagement or a conflict of interest, but not ones you simply disagree with.
  • Google says more reviews and positive ratings can help local ranking, and replying shows you value feedback.
In this article

  2. How fast should a property team reply?

Reply to every apartment review within a day or two, in a calm, specific voice, and move any detail about a resident's account offline. Thank positive reviewers for something they actually said, acknowledge the problem in a negative review without arguing, and flag reviews that break Google's rules instead of debating them in public.

We have covered why reviews matter for leasing before, so this post is the practical part. The example replies are generic templates.

What does Google actually say about replying to reviews?

Google says replying to reviews shows you value your customers and their feedback, and that more reviews and positive ratings can improve local ranking. It does not say replies themselves raise your ranking. Replies are public, posted as your business, and must follow Google's content policies.

That wording comes from Google's page on how to improve local ranking. Google's help page on managing reviews adds three practical points: you need a verified profile to reply, you reply publicly as the business, and its main tone advice is to be nice and stay professional. So I treat replies as a trust signal for the renter reading the page, not a ranking lever. The same goes for AI answers: replies are public text, but Google has not said reply text feeds its AI features, so I would not promise that either.

How fast should a property team reply?

Google does not set a deadline, so pick one your team can keep. We use one to two business days for most reviews and the same day for anything involving safety, an active leak, a lockout or a threat of legal action. Consistency matters more than speed records.

Who should reply?

The community manager should write most replies, because they know whether the work order was closed and can sign with a real role. Reviews about fees, deposits, injuries, discrimination or legal threats should go to the regional manager or legal contact first, before anything is posted.

Keep a short style guide with an approved sign off, an office contact and a list of topics that always escalate.

What should a reply to a positive review say?

Thank the reviewer for one specific thing they mentioned, credit the team member or department if the review named them, and stop. Two to three sentences is enough. Do not add new marketing claims, and do not confirm anything private, such as their unit or move in date.

"Thank you for taking the time to share this. We will pass your note about the fast package room fix along to our maintenance team, who will be glad to hear it. We are happy you are here. The Leasing Team"

If you want to turn good reviews into more than a thank you, our earlier post on going beyond "Thanks for the review" covers that. One caution I would add today: do not repeat a reviewer's name or personal details back to them, even if they are visible.

How should you reply to a maintenance complaint?

Acknowledge the problem in plain words, apologize for the experience without debating the timeline, and give a direct way to reach the person who can fix it. Do not list the work order history in public. The reply is for the next renter as much as for the reviewer.

"We are sorry the repair took longer than it should have. That is not the experience we want for anyone living here. Please call or email our office manager directly so we can confirm the issue is fully resolved. Community Manager"

Avoid "our records show," which reads as an argument and can expose account details.

How should you reply to a noise or neighbor complaint?

Thank the reviewer for raising it, say that you take community living concerns seriously, and invite them to contact the office. Never mention the neighbor, the unit, any lease violation or any action taken against another resident. That information belongs to another household.

"Thank you for letting us know. Everyone deserves to feel comfortable at home, and we take concerns like this seriously. Please reach out to our office directly so we can follow up with you privately. Community Manager"

How should you reply to a review about fees or a deposit dispute?

Keep it short, neutral and private. Acknowledge the frustration, state that you want to review the charges with them directly, and give a contact. Do not quote amounts, lease clauses or ledger history in public, and do not concede that a charge was wrong before the team reviews it.

"We understand how frustrating an unexpected charge can be. We would like to review your statement with you directly. Please contact our office manager at the number on our profile so we can go through it together. Regional Team"

This is not legal advice, and deposit rules vary by state, so have your regional manager or counsel review any reply to a dispute before it is posted.

What should you do about a review that looks fake or comes from a non-resident?

Flag it through your Business Profile if it breaks Google's prohibited and restricted content policy, then post a brief, neutral reply in case it stays up. Google's policy says contributions should reflect a genuine experience and that fake engagement will be removed. Disagreeing with a review is not a reason to flag it.

Google's prohibited and restricted content policy also covers conflicts of interest, including reviews tied to current or former employment, and content posted on a competitor's listing to damage its reputation. Google's page on removing reviews explains how to report one, warns against flagging reviews only because you disagree with them, and describes a one time appeal if your report is rejected. A prospect who toured and left unhappy did have a real experience, so do not assume every non-resident review is fake.

"We take every review seriously, but we could not find a record of this experience with our team. If you have toured or lived here, please contact our office so we can understand what happened. Community Manager"

Do not accuse the reviewer of lying or name a competitor. Report it, reply once, and move on.

What should a reply never say?

Never share private details about a resident, never argue or correct the reviewer point by point, never admit legal liability, and never touch fair housing sensitive topics. Write as if a renter, an owner and an attorney will all read it.

  • Private details. No unit numbers, balances, lease terms, move out dates or anything about other residents.
  • Arguments. Phrases like "actually" or "as we told you" make the community look defensive to every future reader.
  • Liability. Apologize for the experience, not for fault. "We are sorry this happened" is different from "we were negligent." Injury or safety claims always escalate.
  • Fair housing topics. Do not mention or speculate about a resident's family, children, disability, religion, background or any characteristic covered in your fair housing training. If a review alleges discrimination, escalate it before replying.
  • Incentives or pressure. Do not offer anything in exchange for changing a review. Google's policy treats discouraging negative reviews as fake engagement.

Replies are one part of how your community shows up in Google Maps. For the rest of that picture, see how operators win in Google Maps. Reviews are one of the signals we watch in LocalLift, our weekly Google, Maps and AI visibility program for apartment communities.

Questions we hear

How fast should we reply to apartment reviews?

Google does not set a deadline. We aim for one to two business days, and same day for anything about safety or a maintenance issue that is still open.

Should we reply to every review, including five star reviews with no text?

Yes, briefly. Google says replying shows you value your customers and their feedback. A short, specific thank you is enough, and it keeps the page from looking unattended.

Can we get a fake or unfair review removed?

You can flag a review that breaks Google's prohibited and restricted content policy, such as fake engagement or a conflict of interest. Google says not to flag reviews simply because you disagree, so an honest negative review will usually stay.

Do review replies help our Google ranking?

Google's local ranking page says more reviews and positive ratings can help, and that replying shows you value feedback. It does not list replies as a ranking factor, so I would not promise a ranking gain from replies alone.

Who should write our review replies?

The community manager in most cases, using an approved style guide. Anything about fees, deposits, injuries, discrimination or legal threats should go to the regional manager or your legal contact before anyone replies.
